blind/one: Self-attention scores every token against every token, and nothing in a score says where a token sits. Take dog bites man, and one number from each output.
blind/swap: Now swap the first and last words: man bites dog. Every token brings the same query, key and value as before.
blind/same: So bites gets exactly the same output, and dog and man keep theirs too: the outputs just trade places with their tokens.
blind/bag: To attention, a sentence is a bag of tokens. Two sentences with opposite meanings look the same.
add/table: The fix is a second table, P, with one vector per position: row zero for the first token, row one for the second, and so on.
add/sum: Each token's input is its embedding plus the vector for its position. Dog at position zero: one and two, plus zero and one, is one and three.
add/differ: Dog at position two gets one and two, plus one and minus one: two and one. The same word now enters differently in each place, so attention can tell the two sentences apart.
add/learned: The position vectors are learned, like the embeddings. Write T max for the most tokens a model takes: P is T max by d. With one thousand and twenty four tokens of seven hundred sixty eight numbers, that is about seven hundred eighty six thousand learned numbers.
